chapters.title: Composition First

questions.question: How do you build a specialised version of a general component in React?
options: Wrap it and fill in some props
questions.explanation: React has no component inheritance. A specialised component is simply one that renders the general one with certain props already set.

questions.question: How do compound components share state with their children?
options: Through context provided by the parent component
By passing props explicitly at every level
questions.explanation: The parent puts the shared state into a context, so children at any depth can read it while the caller keeps control of the markup.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of cloneElement for injecting props?
options: It only reaches direct children, so wrapping a child in a div breaks it
questions.explanation: `cloneElement` works on the immediate children only. Any extra wrapper element stops the props being delivered, which is why context replaced it.

questions.question: What is a higher order component?
options: A function that takes a component and returns a new enhanced component
A component rendered at the top of the tree
questions.explanation: A HOC wraps a component to add props or behaviour. `React.memo` and `forwardRef` are both examples.

questions.question: Why did custom hooks largely replace HOCs and render props?
options: Hooks share logic without adding wrapper components, injected props or naming collisions
Render props do not work with function components
questions.explanation: Hooks avoid wrapper hell, make the source of a value visible at the call site, and cannot silently collide the way injected props can.

questions.question: How does a component support both controlled and uncontrolled use?
options: By using the prop when it is not undefined and falling back to internal state otherwise
By requiring the caller to pass a mode prop
questions.explanation: Checking whether the value prop is undefined tells the component which mode it is in, exactly as the built-in inputs do.

questions.question: What is the benefit of slot props over a long list of boolean options?
options: Callers supply whatever content they need instead of the component anticipating every variation
Slots are type safe by default
questions.explanation: Composition scales: the component provides structure and the caller provides content, so new variations need no new props.
